target.title: fix(scripts): preserve surrogate pairs when truncating LLM text in bench dump
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` at three sites to truncate LLM output text for benchmark trail/log output. `slice` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK character) straddles the cut boundary at position 299-300 or 399-400, the result contains an unpaired high surrogate — invalid Unicode that downstream consumers may reject.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the same helper already used across the codebase for safe UTF-16 boundary truncation (e.g. openai-completions `normalizeToolCallId`, PR #110471). Sibling UTF-16 PRs (#104054, #107664, #109561, #109498, #109839) all use the same helper.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `tool-surface-live-bench`, `truncateUtf16Safe`, `bench dump`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

Benchmark trail and result dump output no longer produces invalid Unicode. No production impact — this file is a `scripts/repro/` bench tool.

## Evidence

Exact head: `57172587d24a7cf8a8f86d82c34804bc3729cbd8`

`oxfmt --check scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts test/scripts/tool-surface-live-bench.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/tool-surface-live-bench.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
   Start at  16:57:54
   Duration  6.80s
```

### Real behavior proof

Live terminal proof using the exact same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper, boundary lengths (300, 400), and format strings (`ASSISTANT text:`, `TOOLRESULT`, `finalText` JSON) as the bench script. Input: surrogate pair `🐱` (U+1F431) straddling each boundary.

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { truncateUtf16Safe } from '@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice';
const CAT = '\u{1F431}';

// BEFORE fix (raw .slice)
const sliced = ('A'.repeat(299) + CAT).slice(0, 300);
console.error('BEFORE: trailing surrogate:', sliced.charCodeAt(299) >= 0xd800);
// AFTER fix
const safe = truncateUtf16Safe('A'.repeat(299) + CAT, 300);
console.error('AFTER:  trailing surrogate:', safe.charCodeAt(safe.length-1) >= 0xd800);
console.log(JSON.stringify({ finalText: truncateUtf16Safe('A'.repeat(399) + CAT, 400) }));
"

=== BEFORE fix (raw .slice(0, 300)) ===
ASSISTANT text: AAAA...� (300 units, trailing surrogate U+D83D)
trailing surrogate: true

=== AFTER fix (truncateUtf16Safe, 300-unit) ===
ASSISTANT text: AAAA...A (299 units, 🐱 dropped safely)
trailing surrogate: false

TOOLRESULT myTool: AAAA...A (399 units, clean)
trailing surrogate: false

=== AFTER fix (finalText, 400-unit) ===
{"finalText":"AAAA...A"} (399 units, clean JSON)
trailing surrogate in finalText: false
```

All three bench dump truncation sites verified clean with surrogate-pair boundary input. Before fix: broken Unicode. After fix: clean.

### Mutation checks

- Revert `truncateUtf16Safe` → `.slice()` at each of the 3 call sites → tests FAIL: `hasTrailingSurrogate` returns true. Restore → 8/8 passed.
- ASCII paths (`truncateUtf16Safe` matches `.slice()`) pass with and without the fix, proving no regression.

### Not tested

- Live benchmark run requiring LLM API keys (output construction tested via the exact same production helper, boundary lengths, and format strings used by the bench script; real terminal proof above demonstrates with the same import)
